idea_name: Horizon-dependent macro factor set via forward stepwise regression
mechanism: Build a table of US macro calendar releases aligned to EURUSD D1 closes; for each horizon H in {1,5,10} trading days form dependent variable = price change over H; run multiple regression with Forward Stepwise selection and keep only red (p-significant) predictors; the retained factor set and signed b-coefficients become a sensor of which news types currently drive the FX move over that horizon, and the signed R = intercept + Σ b_i * released_value_i forecasts direction/magnitude after publication.
data_needed: Forex Factory (or equivalent) US macro actuals cleaned to numeric columns; EURUSD D1 OHLC; rolling re-fit window as new releases arrive
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD; D1; US macro calendar 2010–mid-2011 (~99 factors, >6700 entries)
why_new_for_mis: MIS can treat the selected factor set and Multiple R as a regime-of-news-impact sensor that flips with horizon (real-estate/Richmond at 1d; production/labor at 5–10d) rather than a static calendar weight list.
quote: When we select as an independent variable the price change in one day after the indicator figures were published, we can see that in the period from 2010 till the middle of 2011 the prices were affected mostly by the data on the sphere of real estate development and indices, published by the Richmond Institute.

idea_name: Spearman rank correlation of Stop Loss series as strategy-redundancy sensor
mechanism: For each strategy keep the sequence of Stop Loss outcomes; compute Spearman's rank-order correlation and its significance (two-/left-/right-sided) between pairs; if Stops1–Stops3 reject H0 of zero correlation while Stops1–Stops2 do not, treat the correlated pair as redundant portfolio sensors and drop one. Same toolkit (Wilcoxon signed-rank, Mann–Whitney U) can sense whether an entry-tweak or broker-execution sample differs in distribution.
data_needed: Per-strategy Stop Loss series; optional broker order-execution-time samples; ALGLIB or equivalent nonparametric tests
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD.e H1 for script demos; generic deal/Stop Loss samples in Data.xls
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a nonparametric sensor of whether two signal streams react to the market the same way on exits—useful for portfolio de-duplication and execution-venue regime checks without assuming normality.
quote: The choice criterion will be as follows: if two strategies are the same at comparing Stop Loss series, then one of the strategies will be removed from the portfolio.

mechanism: Article simulates Labouchere vs fixed-lot betting on a coin with SuccessPercent in {40,49,50,51,55}, PocketPercent, and Take; concludes MM cannot turn non-positive expectation into profit. No market-state sensor is built.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: synthetic coin tosses; no market instrument
why_new_for_mis: No MIS sensing idea after full read—money-management statistical audit only.
quote: No miracle happened. The Labouchere money management system cannot turn a loss-making or even a neutral system into a profitable one.

idea_name: Empirical vs theoretical distribution moments conformity
mechanism: On a return (or other) sample compute MathMean/Variance/Skewness/Kurtosis (excess kurtosis); compare to MathMomentsX theoretical moments of a candidate law (Normal, Lognormal, Student-t, etc.); large deltas flag that the modeled law no longer fits the live sample—usable as a distribution-regime / model-misspecification sensor. Example also uses CDF differences for interval probabilities and quantiles for confidence bands.
data_needed: Rolling array of returns or residuals; chosen parametric family parameters (mu, sigma, …)
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: synthetic Normal(mu=5,sigma=1) demo; library is instrument-agnostic
why_new_for_mis: Exposes a fast in-terminal moment-gap sensor for whether live returns still match the assumed distribution family—foundation for volatility/shape regime flags without leaving MQL5.
quote: In addition, there are functions for calculating theoretical moments of distributions, which allow to evaluate the degree of conformity of the real distribution to the modeled one.

idea_name: Per-symbol and per-ORDER_MAGIC equity plus MFE/MAE excursion maps
mechanism: Replay deal history in timer slices; maintain open-position list and floating profit via CopyTicks; plot Balance/Equity filtered by symbol and DEAL_MAGIC; for each position ID track MFE (max floating profit) and MAE (max floating loss) vs final financial result as scatter sensors of unrealized excursion quality.
data_needed: Account deal history (commission, swap, profit, magic, symbol, entry type); tick cache for mark-to-market; hedge-account multi-EA setup
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD.m, NZDUSD.m examples; history segments of 5–15 minutes; any symbols with positions
why_new_for_mis: Turns multi-strategy account noise into separable contribution and adverse-excursion sensors—MIS can watch which magic/symbol sleeve is driving drawdown or giving back MFE.
quote: Now, you can see the balance and equity statistics per each symbol and magic number on hedge accounts when applying several EAs simultaneously.

mechanism: Educational visualization of Selection/Insertion/Bubble/Quick/Merge/Heap/Radix sorts via CGraphic histograms and multi-indicator threads. No market sensing constructed.
why_new_for_mis: No MIS sensing idea after full read—CS sorting demo only.
quote: My objective is to describe its application areas and consider the process of sorting in details.

idea_name: Drawdown-clustering pd via random yield permutations
mechanism: Given deal yields a_i = (p_exit−p_enter)/(p_enter−p_stop), compute rd for the observed order under minimal-gain constraint d(r)≥D0; then sample many random permutations of the same yields, build the empirical distribution of rd,j, and set pd = fraction with rd,j < rd_observed. Low pd flags that losses are clustered in time (pathological drawdown path); high pd means wins/losses are well mixed—a sensor of path regime of the deal sequence, distinct from Z-score streak counts.
data_needed: Sequence of deal yields a_i with defined stops; D0; Monte Carlo permutations (NT)
why_new_for_mis: Converts deal-path dependence into a probabilistic clustering sensor that tells MIS whether current equity path stress is unusual given the same yield multiset.
quote: pd close to zero indicates a large drawdown caused by loss-making deals gathered close to each other. A pd close to one shows that profitable and loss-making deals were uniformly mixed.

idea_name: Bootstrap δ-quantile of average yield Λ as system-viability sensor
mechanism: Model yields as i.i.d. λ_i; form Λ = mean(λ_1..λ_n); require δ-quantile of Λ ≥ G0 (min average yield vs risk). Estimate via normal approximation (mean A, var S2/n) and/or bootstrap resampling; if q_δ(Λ) < G0, raise nmin or flag system unfit—senses when noise/volatility of outcomes overwhelms required edge.
data_needed: Deal yield sample; G0, δ; bootstrap NB draws
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: same 30-deal sample; nmin≈728 under defaults G0=0.25, δ=0.05
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a statistically gated ‘edge still detectable’ sensor before sizing risk, separating noise-driven underperformance from true regime break.
quote: It is important to make sure that the condition G0≤Λ is broken with probability not greater than δ. For that, the δ quantile of Λ must be no smaller than G0.

idea_name: Parametric exit-family RW-null tests (binomial SL/TP, exponential trail)
mechanism: Under fixed SL/TP ratio k, yields are discrete {−1,k} with θ=Pk; test Mapr>0 against binomial B(n,θ0=1/(1+k)) null of symmetric random walk. Under fixed trailing stop, yields ≈ left-shifted exponential; test Mapr against gamma Γ(n,1/n) null at M=0, estimate θ via MLE, then Monte Carlo ρopt. Rejection of the RW null is a change/edge sensor on the exit process.
data_needed: Deal yields under fixed k or fixed trail Δp; n, δ, G0, D0
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: parametric scripts bn.mq5 / exp.mq5; defaults n=50; continuation of part-1 sample
why_new_for_mis: Turns exit-style assumptions into explicit RW-null sensors so MIS can ask whether observed stop/trail outcomes still look like zero-drift noise.
quote: It is necessary to show that the trades are not a result of trading on a symmetrical random walk. For this, the estimate Mapr must be significantly greater than zero (with reliability δ).

idea_name: Gap overshoot ratio m/g vs Wiener theoretical P(x)=1−1/x
mechanism: For each gap of size g, measure m = max excursion in gap direction until fill; form x=m/g; under discrete-time RW close to Wiener, theoretical CDF is P(x)=0 for x<1 and P(x)=1−1/x for x≥1; compare empirical distribution of x to theory with a goodness-of-fit test—significant excess/deficit of overshoot is a tradable deviation sensor.
data_needed: Gap events with fill path highs/lows; chosen TF for gap definition
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: conceptual in this part; fleshed on EURUSD/USDJPY in follow-on gap article
why_new_for_mis: Provides a path-shape sensor around gaps that is calibrated to an explicit RW null, not just ‘gaps fill’.
quote: Then the random variable x=m/g will have a distribution function close to the function P(x) — such that P(x)=1-1/x if x≥1, and P(x)=0 if x<1.

idea_name: Symbol×direction fixed-lot point-balance as signal-quality / degradation sensor
mechanism: Decompose provider history by symbol and Buy/Sell; plot three series—balance in account currency, balance in points (fixed lot), and lot size. Rising points-balance = genuine edge; rising currency with flat/negative points-balance = lot-manipulation. Optionally run a PriceChannel on the balance curve: break of lower channel → cut lot to minimum (negative scenario); update of upper boundary → restore normal risk.
data_needed: Signal/account trade history with symbol, direction, lots, points PnL; optional balance indicator
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Signal 101185 from Mar 2014: AUDCAD, AUDNZD, EURGBP, EURSGD, GBPCAD, NZDCAD; Buy and Sell separately
why_new_for_mis: MIS can sense per-sleeve edge decay independently of money-management cosmetics, and use balance-channel breaks as regime-change triggers for risk on that sleeve.
quote: If the lower boundary of the price channel is broken through by the balance curve, then it is considered a signal of starting the negative scenario.

idea_name: Spread-percent and dollar-ATR pre-filters for tradable universe
mechanism: Universe scanner hides symbols whose spread/price exceeds thresholds (0.05/0.1/0.15%) or whose 5-day average daily range (ATR in deposit dollars) is below hideATRcents; also filters by session open hour, market-closed today, trade-mode disabled, and existing positions—producing a liquidity- and volatility-screened watchlist plus D1/H1 move% annotations.
data_needed: Broker symbol list or Market Watch; SymbolInfoInteger SPREAD; D1 rates for ATR; session trade times
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: broker stocks/FX/indices; session hours 9am/10am/4pm/midnight; D1 ATR window of 5 bars; chart comment uses D1 and H1
why_new_for_mis: Operationalizes liquidity (relative spread) and short-horizon realized range as first-pass MIS universe sensors before deeper regime models run.
quote: A spread exceeding 0.1% of the price is considered increased. Therefore, we will only display symbols having a spread less than 0.1% by default.

idea_name: Dollar ATR floor as intraday-volatility eligibility sensor
mechanism: CopyRates D1 for last 5 completed bars; atr = mean(high−low); drop symbol if 0 < atr < hideATRcents—so instruments that statistically cannot deliver the trader’s required dollar move are excluded from the sensed opportunity set.
data_needed: D1 OHLC per symbol; configured minimum dollar range
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: any broker symbols; PERIOD_D1; 5-bar mean range
why_new_for_mis: Simple realized-volatility gate in price units MIS can reuse as a binary ‘enough movement’ sensor across equities and FX.
quote: If you trade intraday and wait for the price to move for at least 50-90 cents, you are unlikely to need symbols that statistically move for no more than 30 cents per day.

idea_name: Gap Q-statistic empirical CDF vs uniform RW null (KS)
mechanism: On each gap define p0 (post-gap), p1 (pre-gap/stop side), p2 (farthest price before fill); Q=(p2−p0)/(p2−p1) ∈[0,1). Under zero-drift Wiener, Q ~ Uniform[0,1]. Build empirical Fq from last N gaps (ticks, minute bars, or sessions); Kolmogorov–Smirnov p-value vs uniform; where Fq(q)≪q favor fade-the-gap, where Fq(q)≫q favor continuation; map q to expected M_cont / M_rvrs including spread.
data_needed: Tick or OHLC series; gmin; optional session period/length/bias; R or equivalent for KS
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD and USDJPY; consecutive ticks, 1-minute bars, American (EURUSD) / Tokyo (USDJPY) sessions; last 50 and 200 gaps
why_new_for_mis: Concrete, instrumented RW-deviation sensor on gap aftermath that MIS can run continuously to detect when gap-fill behavior leaves the martingale null.
quote: If Fq(x) is significantly different from the theoretical distribution function with a random walk Fq0(x), we need to check the significance of this difference in terms of profitability.

idea_name: Homework tabs and chart-object persistence UI
mechanism: Extends the symbol-nav utility with Long/Short/Range tabs, file persistence, and save/load of graphical objects; Finviz ticker import for external prefilter. After full read, no new market sensing mechanism beyond UI/workflow around filters already extracted from 5348.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: same utility; optional finviz.com screener tickers / symbols.txt
why_new_for_mis: No new MIS sensing idea after full read—UI and homework-list persistence for the prior scanner.
quote: In this article, we will save trees from destruction and will learn how to automatically save graphical objects created on a chart so that you do not have to constantly create them in the future.
